title: Local realization of a finitely presented module at a site point
statement: Let $C$ be a site small in the coefficient universe and having finite limits [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $C$, let $p:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(C)$ be a point [def-trf-geometric-morphism], and set $R_p=p^{-1}R$. Let $M$ be a finitely presented $R_p$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. There exist an object $U$ of $C$, an element $x\in p^{-1}(h_U^\#)$, and a sheaf $F$ of $R_U$-modules on the localized site $C/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with the following properties. Here $h_U(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_C(V,U)$ and $h_U^\#$ is its sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. The element $x$ specifies a point $q:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(C/U)$ with $j_Uq\cong p$, where $j_U^{-1}$ is restriction to $C/U$. There are canonical identifications $q^{-1}R_U\cong R_p$ and $q^{-1}(G|_U)\cong p^{-1}G$, natural in all $R$-module sheaves $G$, and an $R_p$-linear isomorphism $q^{-1}F\cong M$. The sheaf $F$ can be chosen as the cokernel of a map $R_U^a\to R_U^b$ given by a finite matrix with entries in $R(U)$, for some natural numbers $a,b$.

source.place: Tag 0DEN, lemma-check-K-flat-stalks, proof of (1), paragraph beginning Let M be a finitely presented O_p-module: local finite-presentation realization and restriction to C/U. This statement isolates the local algebra and slice-point construction, without any K-flatness assertion.

proof.text: Apply the site-point reconstruction theorem to $p$. Put $u(V)=p^{-1}(h_V^\#)$ and let $\mathcal N$ have objects $(V,y)$ with $y\in u(V)$ and arrows preserving these elements. It is small and cofiltered, and for every sheaf of sets $G$ its canonical section-to-germ map identifies $p^{-1}G$ with $\varinjlim_{\mathcal N^{\mathrm{op}}}G(V)$. In particular every element of the underlying set of $R_p$ is represented by a section of $R$ on a pointed object. Only this set-valued assertion is used: no constant-coefficient hypothesis on $R$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0DEN, lemma-check-K-flat-stalks, proof of (1), local finite-presentation realization paragraph.

proof.text: By finite presentation choose $a,b\in\mathbf N$ and an exact presentation $R_p^a\xrightarrow A R_p^b\to M\to0$. Write the linear map in the standard bases as the finite matrix $(A_{ij})_{i<b,j<a}$. For each entry, step 1 supplies a pointed object $(U_{ij},x_{ij})$ and a section representing it. Cofilteredness supplies a common pointed object $(U,x)$ with arrows to these finitely many objects. Restrict the chosen sections along these arrows to obtain $r_{ij}\in R(U)$ whose germs are $A_{ij}$. If $ab=0$, choose any object of the nonempty category $\mathcal N$ and take the empty matrix. The germ map $R(U)\to R_p$ is a ring homomorphism: a section is a sheaf map $h_U^\#\to R$, and applying the finite-product-preserving $p^{-1}$ to the addition and multiplication identities sends its value at $x$ to the corresponding sum or product of germs. Thus the lifted matrix maps to $A$ as a matrix over rings.

source.place: Tag 0DEN, lemma-check-K-flat-stalks, proof of (1), local finite-presentation realization paragraph.

proof.text: Set $H=h_U^\#$ and $S=p^{-1}H$, so $x\in S$. The slice-equivalence theorem gives $E_U:\operatorname{Sh}(C/U)\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(C)/H$. The sheaf-limit theorem supplies finite limits in $\operatorname{Sh}(C)$, and the slice-adjoint lemma applied to $p^{-1}\dashv p_*$ gives a finite-limit-preserving left adjoint $P:\operatorname{Sh}(C)/H\to\mathbf{Set}/S$, acting by $p^{-1}$ on arrows. Define $e_x:\mathbf{Set}/S\to\mathbf{Set}$ by taking the fibre over $x$. This preserves finite limits, computed fibre by fibre. It has the explicit right adjoint assigning to a set $B$ the family with fibre $B$ at $x$ and a singleton at every $s\ne x$: a map into that family is exactly a map from the $x$-fibre into $B$. Equivalences have their inverse as right adjoint and preserve limits. Hence $q^{-1}=e_x\circ P\circ E_U$ has a right adjoint (compose the three right adjoints in reverse order) and preserves finite limits. It defines a geometric morphism $q:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(C/U)$.

source.place: Tag 04H2, lemma-point-localize; explicit slice-adjunction construction using Tag 04H1, lemma-localize-morphism-topoi, and Tag 00Y1, lemma-essential-image-j-shriek.

proof.text: For a set sheaf $G$, the quasi-inverse formula for $E_U$ sends $(G\times H\to H)$ at an object $v:V\to U$ to the fibre of $G(V)\times H(V)\to H(V)$ over $\eta(v)$, canonically $G(V)$. Thus $E_U(G|_U)\cong(G\times H\to H)$, naturally in $G$. Applying $P$ gives $(p^{-1}G\times S\to S)$, because $p^{-1}$ preserves products, and applying $e_x$ gives the projection isomorphism $q^{-1}(G|_U)\cong p^{-1}G$. These natural identifications give $j_Uq\cong p$. Applied to the zero, unit, addition, multiplication and module-action maps, the same product identifications respect all operations. Consequently they identify $q^{-1}R_U$ with $R_p$ as rings and $q^{-1}(G|_U)$ with $p^{-1}G$ as $R_p$-modules, naturally in module sheaves $G$. For a section $r\in R(U)$ its image under this ring identification is its germ $p^{-1}(r)(x)$: under $E_U$ the corresponding section of $R_U$ is the graph of $r:H\to R$, and taking its $x$-fibre after $p^{-1}$ evaluates exactly at $x$. This checks the coefficient map used for the lifted matrix.

source.place: Tag 04H2, lemma-point-localize, equality of stalk functors; Tag 00Y1, lemma-essential-image-j-shriek, explicit fibre formula.

proof.text: On $C/U$ define $\alpha:R_U^a\to R_U^b$ at $v:V\to U$ by $(t_j)_j\mapsto(\sum_j r_{ij}|_V\,t_j)_i$. Restriction maps preserve these sums and products, so this is a morphism of module sheaves. Form its sheaf cokernel $F=\operatorname{coker}(\alpha)$ in the abelian module-sheaf category. For the geometric morphism $q$, transported module inverse image preserves cokernels. It also identifies $q^{-1}(R_U^n)$ with $R_p^n$ for each finite $n$, since these powers are finite products and $q^{-1}$ preserves finite limits (including the zero module when $n=0$). The coefficient calculation in step 4 identifies $q^{-1}\alpha$ with $A$: on a tuple its $i$th coordinate is $\sum_j A_{ij}t_j$. Therefore $q^{-1}F\cong\operatorname{coker}(A)\cong M$ as $R_p$-modules, by the chosen exact presentation. This proves the assertion with the actual finite matrix $(r_{ij})$ over $R(U)$.
